guide.universaloreprocessing.grind.1: Right-click a vanilla grindstone with clumps. Each click grinds one clump into one dust. A hopper above the grindstone feeds it, and the dust drops out below.
guide.universaloreprocessing.grind.2: Clumps that were washed stay washed as dust.
guide.universaloreprocessing.grind.3: Fill a Quern with up to a stack of clumps, by hand or from a hopper above. Turn it with an empty hand or a redstone pulse; the peg on the top stone moves a quarter turn and one dust leaves through the spout.
guide.universaloreprocessing.grind.4: A Quern holds one material at a time. Grind it empty before switching.
guide.universaloreprocessing.grind.diagr: A hopper above feeds clumps; a lever turns the stone; a hopper below catches the dust. Without a container below, the dust spills from the spout.
guide.universaloreprocessing.grind.mista: Grinding raw ore: it is too hard. Strike it into clumps first.
Adding a second material to a Quern that still holds the first.
Turning an empty Quern: nothing comes out.
guide.universaloreprocessing.grind.waste: For every %s clumps ground, one %s of rock comes out with the dust.
guide.universaloreprocessing.intro.1: Ore can be smelted as it comes, or carried up a ladder of physical steps first. Each step is done by hand in the world, and each one raises what the ore smelts into.
guide.universaloreprocessing.intro.2: Strike raw ore into clumps, grind clumps into dust, stir dust into slurry, and let the slurry settle into shards. Any form can be smelted at any time; the higher the form, the more metal it gives.
guide.universaloreprocessing.intro.3: Every step has a machine that does the same work in bulk or from redstone. The machines are introduced in the chapter of the step they serve.
guide.universaloreprocessing.intro.4: Hover over an item in this book to see its name. When something does not work, a short note appears above the hotbar saying why; the last chapter lists them all.
guide.universaloreprocessing.settle.1: Once stirred, the slurry settles on its own in about %s seconds. The surface clears, then crystals grow on it in three visible stages.
guide.universaloreprocessing.settle.2: When the third stage of crystals shows, right-click to collect the shards. The cauldron is left empty.
guide.universaloreprocessing.settle.3: A Settling Tank works like a cauldron that holds %s dust. Fill it with a water bucket, add dust, stir it, and wait. Hoppers may add dust from the side or top and take the shards and clay out from below.
guide.universaloreprocessing.settle.4: The water is used up by the slurry. Refill the tank for the next batch.
guide.universaloreprocessing.settle.diag: A hopper feeds dust from the side, a paddle stirs from above, and a hopper below collects the shards and clay.
guide.universaloreprocessing.settle.mist: Collecting too early: wait for the third crystal stage.
Adding dust to a dry tank: fill it with water first.
Adding dust after stirring: start a new batch once the shards are collected.
guide.universaloreprocessing.settle.wast: The finest rock sinks under the crystals. For every %s dust settled you also collect one %s with the shards.
guide.universaloreprocessing.smelt.1: Every form smelts in a furnace or blast furnace. Higher forms give more:
guide.universaloreprocessing.smelt.2: Fractions are never lost to chance. A stack keeps a running total, so four clumps always give exactly five ingots.
guide.universaloreprocessing.smelt.3: Shards are the end of the ladder. Smelt them.
guide.universaloreprocessing.stir.1: Fill a cauldron to the brim with water and drop in dust. Add more dust of the same material, then stir with a stick.
guide.universaloreprocessing.stir.2: A cauldron holds up to %s dust. It turns to slurry after %s stirs.
guide.universaloreprocessing.stir.3: A Stirring Paddle rests on the rim of a cauldron or Settling Tank. Each redstone pulse, or a right-click with an empty hand, swings the paddle once and gives one stir.
guide.universaloreprocessing.stir.diagra: A Stirring Paddle on a cauldron, worked by a lever.
guide.universaloreprocessing.stir.mistak: Adding dust to a cauldron that is not completely full of water.
Adding clumps or raw ore: only dust stays suspended.
Mixing two materials in one cauldron.
guide.universaloreprocessing.strike.1: Place a raw ore or an ore block on a Crushing Slab, then strike it with a Hammer.
guide.universaloreprocessing.strike.2: It breaks after %s strikes. The floor of the slab wears from smooth stone toward cobblestone during the last strikes, so you can see how close it is. The clumps pop out on top of the slab.
guide.universaloreprocessing.strike.3: Set a Trip Hammer directly on top of a Crushing Slab. Each redstone pulse drops the head for one strike. A clock or a lever flicked by hand both work.
guide.universaloreprocessing.strike.4: A falling anvil also strikes a slab it lands on, one strike per fall.
guide.universaloreprocessing.strike.diag: An anvil dropped onto a Crushing Slab.
A lever beside the Trip Hammer, the Crushing Slab below it.
guide.universaloreprocessing.strike.mist: Striking an empty slab: place the ore first.
Putting a Trip Hammer beside the slab: it must sit directly on top.
Putting clumps back on the slab: they are already crushed. Grind them.
guide.universaloreprocessing.strike.wast: Ore is never pure metal. For every %s items broken, the rock around the metal is left behind as one %s, popped out with the clumps.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.1.f: Place raw ore or an ore block on the slab first. Only one item rests on it at a time.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.1.p: Nothing happens when I strike the slab.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.2.f: Only clumps can be ground. Strike raw ore on a Crushing Slab first.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.2.p: The grindstone or Quern will not take my ore.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.3.f: The cauldron must be full of water, and all its dust must be one material.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.3.p: Dust will not go into the cauldron.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.4.f: It needs to be stirred first, then left until the third crystal stage shows.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.4.p: The slurry will not give shards.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.5.f: Each Sluice must be waterlogged, and all must face the same way.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.5.p: Items float straight over my Sluices.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.6.f: It works on the block directly below it, and that block needs something to work on.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.6.p: My Trip Hammer or Stirring Paddle only makes a dull knock.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.7.f: Stand in water and hold unwashed clumps or dust in your other hand.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.8.f: Check that ladder smelting is enabled in the config, and that the material is not excluded.
guide.universaloreprocessing.trouble.int: Each note below matches a message shown above the hotbar.
guide.universaloreprocessing.wash.1: Washing is optional. Lay Sluices in a straight row, all facing the same way, and pour a water bucket into each one. Drop clumps or dust in: they sink, crawl downstream and tumble over each riffle.
guide.universaloreprocessing.wash.2: As an item clears the last riffle of the row it is washed, and may give byproducts. Longer rows raise the chance, up to %s Sluices.
guide.universaloreprocessing.wash.3: Before you have a Sluice row, stand in water with clumps or dust in your other hand and hold use with a Panning Tray. It washes the stack as a row of one Sluice.
guide.universaloreprocessing.wash.byprod: Base chances for %s, per item per Sluice: %s.
%s has no byproducts in the current tables.
guide.universaloreprocessing.wash.diagra: Four Sluices in a row, each holding water. Items travel the way the Sluices face.
guide.universaloreprocessing.wash.mistak: Leaving the Sluices dry: they only carry ore when waterlogged.
Turning one Sluice the other way: the row ends where the direction changes.
Washing the same stack twice: each stack is washed only once.
hint.universaloreprocessing.cauldron.not: Fill the cauldron to the brim with water first.
hint.universaloreprocessing.cauldron.too: Too coarse to suspend in water. Grind it into dust first.
hint.universaloreprocessing.grind.done: Already ground. Stir dust into a full water cauldron.
hint.universaloreprocessing.grind.raw: Too hard to grind. Strike it into clumps on a Crushing Slab first.
hint.universaloreprocessing.paddle.no_ve: A Stirring Paddle stirs the block below it. Place it on a cauldron or Settling Tank.
hint.universaloreprocessing.paddle.nothi: There is no unstirred slurry below the paddle.
hint.universaloreprocessing.quern.empty: The quern is empty. Add clumps, then turn it.
hint.universaloreprocessing.quern.other_: The quern still holds %s. Grind those first.
hint.universaloreprocessing.slab.empty: The slab is empty. Place raw ore on it first, then strike.
hint.universaloreprocessing.slab.occupie: The slab already holds %s. Take it off with an empty hand.
hint.universaloreprocessing.sluice.dry: A Sluice only carries ore when waterlogged. Pour a water bucket into it.
hint.universaloreprocessing.sluice.facin: Sluices in a row must all face the same way.
hint.universaloreprocessing.slurry.full: It holds all the dust it can (%s). Stir it now.
hint.universaloreprocessing.slurry.needs: Stir the slurry with a stick or a Stirring Paddle.
hint.universaloreprocessing.slurry.other: This holds %s slurry. Let it settle before adding %s.
hint.universaloreprocessing.slurry.settl: Settling: stage %s of %s. Leave it undisturbed.
hint.universaloreprocessing.slurry.wrong: Only dust can be stirred into slurry.
hint.universaloreprocessing.tank.full: The tank holds all the dust it can. Stir it now.
hint.universaloreprocessing.tank.no_dust: Add dust to the water before stirring.
hint.universaloreprocessing.tank.no_wate: Fill the tank with a water bucket first.
hint.universaloreprocessing.tray.no_load: Hold clumps or dust in your other hand to pan them.
hint.universaloreprocessing.tray.washed: That stack has already been washed.
A Trip Hammer strikes the block directly below it. Place it on a Crushing Slab.
